identity_model.before: FunctionIdentity carried repository/revision/language/scope/symbol/span/generated only. Disambiguation across free functions, nested modules, inherent methods, trait declarations/defaults/implementations, associated functions and generic declarations existed ONLY as an incidental side effect of the Rust extractor's scope-string encoding (e.g. a SemanticScope segment literally spelled "impl:Reader for Foo" or "trait:Reader") -- the typed kernel itself had no field answering "is this a trait implementation method" or "what impl/trait owns this method" without re-parsing that string. Additionally, function_identity() unconditionally hardcoded symbol.role = SymbolRole::Definition, so a trait method DECLARATION (no body) incoherently claimed Definition inside its own FunctionIdentity even though the separately-emitted Symbol observation for the same declaration correctly recorded Declaration.
identity_model.after: FunctionIdentity gains three new typed fields, all participating in identity_key(): declaration_kind: FunctionDeclarationKind (FreeFunction/InherentMethod/AssociatedFunction/TraitMethodDeclaration/TraitDefaultMethod/TraitImplementationMethod), owner: FunctionOwner { target: Option<TypeIdentity>, trait_path: Option<String> } (syntactically-observed impl self type and/or trait path -- never a compiler-resolved DefId), and generics: Vec<String> (this function's own declared generic parameters, source-spelling order). SemanticRecordId/record_id() itself, and every family's identity_key() call chain, remain the exact same kind of deterministic string-hash mechanism used throughout R4 -- no new identity *mechanism* was introduced, only new *fields* feeding the existing one. FunctionSignature embeds FunctionIdentity directly, so it inherits the strengthening automatically with zero changes to its own struct. The symbol.role coherence bug is fixed: the correct role (Declaration for a trait method with no body, Definition otherwise) now flows into both the Symbol observation and the embedded FunctionIdentity.symbol.role consistently.

declaration_kinds_implemented: FreeFunction -- top-level or nested-module function, not inside impl/trait
InherentMethod -- impl Type { fn foo(&self) } -- has a self/&self/&mut self receiver
AssociatedFunction -- impl Type { fn foo() } -- no receiver (e.g. Type::new())
TraitMethodDeclaration -- trait Name { fn foo(&self); } -- no body
TraitDefaultMethod -- trait Name { fn foo(&self) { .. } } -- has a default body
TraitImplementationMethod -- impl Trait for Type { fn foo(&self) { .. } }, receiver or not

owner_trait_model.representation: FunctionOwner { target: Option<TypeIdentity>, trait_path: Option<String> }. target is Some(<impl self type>) whenever the function is declared inside any impl block (inherent or trait impl); None for a free function or a trait-declared method (which has no impl target -- the trait itself is named via trait_path). trait_path is Some(<trait name/path as syntactically written>) for a trait declaration/default method (the enclosing trait) and for a trait impl method (the impl's `for <Trait>` clause); None for a free function or an inherent method.
owner_trait_model.epistemic_discipline: Both fields are always a literal source-level spelling (identical in kind to TypeIdentity.name), never a compiler-resolved identity. A trait declaration (owner.target=None, trait_path=Some("Reader")) and its implementation (owner.target=Some("Foo"), trait_path=Some("Reader")) are ALWAYS represented as two distinct FunctionIdentity values with two distinct identity_key()s -- R4.4 never asserts they are the 'same' function, only that the shared trait_path string is an observable source-level relationship between them. Whether that implementation is compiler-provably the canonical implementation of that trait declaration remains an explicit reconciliation-owned relation, never claimed at extraction time.
owner_trait_model.no_fuzzy_merge: No identity is ever synthesized from name equality, signature equality, display-string equality, span-shape similarity or model judgment. Every distinguishing field (declaration_kind, owner.target, owner.trait_path, generics, scope, span, revision) is either literally present in the syn AST or explicitly None/empty when source syntax does not supply it.

generics: FunctionIdentity.generics: Vec<String> -- the function's OWN declared generic parameters (e.g. ["T", "U: Clone"]), in source declaration order, computed once per function and shared between FunctionIdentity and the pre-existing FunctionSignature.generics (previously computed twice, now computed once and cloned). Never a monomorphized instance identity (e.g. convert::<u32>() is explicitly out of scope, R4.5+ territory). Enclosing impl-block/trait-block generic parameter LISTS (the `<T>` in `impl<T> Foo<T> for Bar<T>`) are not separately captured as their own field this wave -- they already participate indirectly via the self-type/trait-path spellings (`spelling::type_spelling`/`path_spelling` render a type's own generic ARGUMENTS, e.g. "Bar<T>"/"Foo<T>", inline), which is sufficient for the required test matrix (all of which test a function's OWN generics) but is noted below as unmodeled surface for a future wave.

revision_scope_rules.revision: FunctionIdentity.revision (and the embedded SymbolIdentity.revision) remain first-class identity fields, unchanged in kind from pre-R4.4; a revision change alone still changes identity_key() (re-confirmed by a dedicated R4.4-corpus test in addition to the pre-existing R4.3 one).
revision_scope_rules.scope: SemanticScope segment accumulation (module nesting, still including the pre-existing "impl:X"/"trait:X" string segments for backward compatibility and human-readable grouping) is unchanged; it remains source-syntax-derived, never traversal-order- or HashMap-iteration-derived.
revision_scope_rules.repository_first_class: FunctionIdentity.repository (a RepositoryId, distinct from RevisionRef) was already first-class before this wave and remains so; no function is assumed to belong to a single implicit root repository, so functions discovered later in a dependency-expanded corpus (R4's separate, NOT-implemented-this-wave DEPENDENCY-CENSUS.md capability) remain globally distinguishable by (repository, revision, ...) without redesign.

epistemic_limits.what_source_proves: Which impl block a method is declared inside (self type spelling); whether that impl syntactically names a trait, and which one; whether a trait method has a default body; whether a method has a receiver; a function's own declared generic parameters; module/scope nesting; the exact source span.
epistemic_limits.what_remains_unresolved: Whether a trait impl is the compiler-canonical implementation of a given trait declaration (no rustc name resolution is performed); whether two differently-spelled impl targets denote the same underlying type (e.g. via a type alias) -- TypeIdentity.canonical stays None throughout, exactly as in R4.3; monomorphized/instantiated generic identities (e.g. convert::<u32>) -- not modeled; macro-expanded declarations -- never fabricated, only what syn parses directly from source is ever emitted; full compiler DefId-level resolution -- not claimed anywhere.

pipeline_losslessness.normalization_to_graph: add_typed_semantic_nodes()'s FunctionIdentity arm already (from R4.3.3) keys the graph node id on header.record_id.as_str() -- since record_id is derived from the now-strengthened identity_key(), distinct strengthened FunctionIdentity values automatically produce distinct graph nodes with ZERO graph code changes required this wave; only new tests were added to prove it.

multi_extractor_proof.claim: Two independent extractors reporting the identical strengthened FunctionIdentity claim (same repository/revision/scope/symbol/span/declaration_kind/owner/generics) both survive Census and Normalization as two independent typed_semantic_records entries.
multi_extractor_proof.mechanism: record_id() (built from the now-strengthened identity_key()) is identical for both observations, proving the semantic CLAIM identity is unaffected by which extractor reported it; raw_observation_id() (which additionally hashes extractor id/version, status, evidence_refs, provenance and the full typed payload) differs between the two, so R4.3.3's raw_observation_id-keyed dedup (unmodified this wave) correctly keeps both.

verification_passes.contract_judgment: Independently read SEMANTIC-EXTRACTION.md and NORMALIZATION.md. NORMALIZATION.md#identity explicitly forbids "same display name"/"unqualified text" as an equivalence proof and lists declaration identity as an allowed scoping component; SEMANTIC-EXTRACTION.md forbids inventing facts or compiler-resolved semantics. FunctionOwner's framing (syntactic-only, source-spelling, no DefId, no claim that a trait declaration and its implementation are "the same" function) was judged consistent with both -- it adds identity-scoping, not equivalence, and correctly defers "does this impl canonically implement that trait method" to reconciliation.

No Default impl/derive on FunctionIdentity; the sole production constructor (adapter/src/semantic/rust/mod.rs::function_identity) explicitly threads declaration_kind/owner/generics on every call -- no silent-default gap.
verification_passes.verdict: VERIFIED -- production identity/Census/graph mechanism confirmed correct and load-bearing (E, F); one test-assertion ambiguity found (D) and fixed; no production defects found.

runtime_invariants_established: FunctionIdentity.identity_key() now distinguishes: (1) same name, different modules; (2) same method name, different inherent impl owners; (3) an inherent method vs. a trait-impl method of the same name on the same owner; (4) two different traits implementing the same method name on the same owner; (5) a trait method declaration vs. its default-bodied sibling (both by declaration_kind and by the now-coherent symbol.role); (6) an associated function (no receiver) vs. a receiver method of the same owner; (7) distinct generic parameter lists on an otherwise-identical declaration -- all via typed structure (declaration_kind/owner/generics), confirmed load-bearing in isolation at the core-record level (independent of any scope-string redundancy the Rust extractor also happens to retain).
FunctionSignature automatically inherits every one of the above through its embedded FunctionIdentity, with zero changes to FunctionSignature's own struct or identity_key() call chain.

The R4.3.3 raw-observation-vs-semantic-claim identity separation is unmodified and re-confirmed under the strengthened model: two independent extractors reporting the identical strengthened FunctionIdentity claim share record_id (the claim) while differing in raw_observation_id (the per-extractor attribution), so neither can silently overwrite the other through Census or Normalization.

The engineering graph's FunctionIdentity nodes are keyed on the now-strengthened record_id with no graph code changes required, so two FunctionIdentity records differing only in owner automatically produce two distinct graph nodes -- proven by a dedicated test, not merely assumed from the R4.3.3 mechanism carrying over.
contract_clauses_satisfied: .atlas/contracts/SEMANTIC-EXTRACTION.md (function/method identity closure: every discovered function/method now carries a stable, scope-and-owner-correct identity rather than a name-only or scope-string-incidental one; no monomorphized/compiler-resolved identity is fabricated)

.atlas/contracts/NORMALIZATION.md#identity ("Name equality is not identity equality": two methods named `read`/`get`/`execute` on different owners, or via different traits, are provably distinct FunctionIdentity values; no equivalence is asserted between a trait declaration and its implementation without compiler-provided evidence)

.atlas/decisions/0002-epistemic-status-model.md (FunctionIdentity's new owner/declaration_kind fields carry only what source syntax can literally prove; no field claims OBSERVED-grade certainty about compiler-resolved trait/impl equivalence)

.atlas/architecture/CAPABILITY-ARCHITECTURE.md (typed identity/relation/schema/epistemic-status/revision-scope primitives live under core/semantic + core/schema, not as a parallel adapter/runtime taxonomy -- FunctionDeclarationKind and FunctionOwner were added under core/src/semantic/function.rs, not duplicated in adapter or runtime)
still_unsupported: CALL -- no call-target resolution, call graph, or SemanticObservation::Call output from Rust extraction; this wave deliberately stops at identity, not the call relation itself.
CONTROL_FLOW / DATA_FLOW / STATE / EFFECT / OWNERSHIP / CONCURRENCY / PERSISTENCE -- unmaterialized, unchanged from R4.3.3.

Transitive dependency census runtime (.atlas/contracts/DEPENDENCY-CENSUS.md) -- explicitly out of scope this wave; FunctionIdentity.repository remains first-class so dependency-expanded-corpus functions remain distinguishable when that capability is built, but no dependency resolution logic was added.
Full compiler/global Rust name resolution -- no rustc, no HIR/MIR, no trait solving, no macro expansion; declaration_kind/owner are always syntactic-only conclusions.
Monomorphized/instantiated generic identity (e.g. convert::<u32>) -- not modeled; FunctionIdentity.generics captures only the function's own declared parameter list.

Impl-block-level and trait-block-level generic parameter LISTS (the `<T>` in `impl<T> Foo<T> for Bar<T>` / `trait Foo<T>`) are not captured as their own explicit field -- they participate only indirectly via the self-type/trait-path spellings already rendering generic arguments inline. Sufficient for this wave's required test matrix (all of which exercise a function's own generics) but noted as unmodeled surface for a future wave if impl/trait-level generic identity ever needs independent disambiguation.

Reconciliation of a trait declaration with its implementation(s) into one provably-equivalent relation -- remains an explicit, unimplemented reconciliation-owned relation; R4.4 only guarantees the two stay distinct AND that their observable trait_path relationship survives.

The Rust extractor's pre-existing scope-string encoding (e.g. a SemanticScope segment literally spelling "impl:Reader for Foo") was deliberately RETAINED alongside the new typed owner/declaration_kind fields rather than removed, per this wave's smallest-coherent-evolution scope. Independent verification confirmed this means the new typed fields are proven load-bearing in isolation only at the core-record level (hand-built FunctionIdentity literals) and at the Census/graph consumer level (raw_observation_id dedup, graph node keying) -- not by the adapter-level tests running against real extractor output, which currently pass via a redundant combination of scope-string and span disambiguation as well as the new fields. Removing the now-redundant scope-string encoding (or adding adapter-level tests that neutralize it to isolate owner/declaration_kind specifically) is unstarted future cleanup, not required by this wave's acceptance criteria.
